name: Andharban Jungle Trail
tagline: Widely called one of India's best jungle treks — a point-to-point descent through the 'Amazon of Maharashtra'
seoTitle: Andharban Jungle Trail Solo Trek Guide — The Solo Trail
seoDescription: Solo trekker's guide to the Andharban Jungle Trail near Pune — one of India's best-rated jungle treks. Logistics note: this is point-to-point, not a loop.

seasons.label: Jun – Sep
seasons.sub: Monsoon — canopy lushest, waterfalls at full force

seasons.label: Feb – May
seasons.sub: Dry, less scenic, water sources reduced

routeOptions.name: Pimpri to Bhira Dam (standard descent)
routeOptions.notes: A gentle net descent, but includes stream crossings and slippery rocky sections that require reasonable fitness. This is point-to-point — you'll need return transport arranged at the Bhira end, since it does not loop back to the start.

safety.intro: Andharban's main technical hazard is stream crossings that can become genuinely hazardous when water is running high in heavy monsoon.

alerts.title: Stream crossings can become hazardous in high water
alerts.body: This is a jungle descent with multiple stream crossings. In heavy monsoon downpours, water levels can rise quickly — do not attempt a crossing if the water looks fast or thigh-deep. Wait it out or turn back.

cards.title: Before you go
items: This is point-to-point, not a loop — arrange a vehicle/driver to meet you at Bhira Dam before you start
Check recent rainfall — heavy rain can raise stream levels significantly

cards.title: On the trail
items: Rocky sections get very slippery — grippy footwear matters more than speed
No mobile signal for long stretches — download offline maps beforehand

cards.title: Solo-specific
items: Popular enough on weekends that you'll likely have other trekkers around
Weekday solo attempts should ideally still coordinate a pickup contact who knows your timeline
Leech socks recommended for monsoon — this is genuine jungle terrain

items.name: Grippy trekking shoes (essential for wet rock and stream crossings)
Quick-dry clothing — you will get wet
Leech socks for monsoon jungle sections
Offline map/GPX — no signal for long stretches
